newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up on speculative buying.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended up thanks to speculative buying just before the close, but trading was dull on gloomy market sentiment, brokers said.
The index gained 0.250 points or 0.50 percent to 50.402 points, on volume of 3.9 million shares worth $1.6 millon. Of 41 B shares, 31 traded, with 10 up, eight flat and 13 down.
Brokers said speculative buying in selective stocks in the last minutes reversed early losses, but sentiment was still weak without a clear market direction.

"After consecutive falls over the past few weeks, the rise was to be expected from a technical point of view," one broker said. "But the thin volume indicated that the downward trend will continue in the short term if there is no positive news."
"The 50-point support level will be breached on current market conditions, and a further fall of 5-7 percent will be possible," a second broker said.
Shanghai Jintai performed the best, surging $0.024 or 17.91 percent to $0.158 on volume of 5,000 shares.
Eastern Communications also surged, rising $0.060 or 8.33 percent to $0.780 on volume of 154,700 shares.
Shanghai Worldbest traded the most on overseas institutional unwinding selling and domestic institutional support. It ended unchanged at $0.780 on volume of 516,300 shares.
Shanghai A shares closed down on cautious market sentiment, brokers said.
The A index shed 0.951 points or 0.12 percent to 813.649 points, on volume of 281.2 million shares worth 2.7 billion yuan. The SSE 30 gained 9.596 points or 0.46 percent to 2087.640 points.
Ninbo Hualian was the biggest loser, falling 1.08 yuan or 7.25 percent to 13.80 yuan on volume of 415,800 shares.
